security_audit.summary: Most static external-command detections are false positives caused by Markdown fences or inline code formatting. The real risks are the generated shell scripts, privileged host network changes, proxy environment modification, and a live blocked-domain test that may contact an untrusted domain if controls fail.

remediation.issue: Generated configuration script changes host firewall and system files.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit confirmation steps, dry-run output, backups, rollback commands, and a requirement to test only in disposable or sandboxed environments.

remediation.issue: The test script uses malicious.com as a live blocked-domain target.
remediation.suggestion: Replace it with a controlled internal test host, a reserved documentation domain, or a local mock that cannot send traffic to an untrusted site.

remediation.issue: The generated environment file clears HTTPS_PROXY.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid overriding HTTPS_PROXY by default and document how to preserve required organizational proxy settings.

content.user_title: Configure Network Security for Claude Code
content.value_statement: AI coding sandboxes need clear network boundaries to reduce accidental exposure. This skill provides a structured workflow for trusted domains, access rules, validation, and documentation.
actual_capabilities: Documents required external dependencies, ports, protocols, and rate limits for a sandbox.
Defines a whitelist-based network policy with trusted and blocked domains.
Shows example firewall, DNS filtering, proxy, and environment variable configuration steps.
Creates validation steps for trusted domain access, blocked domain checks, and local port checks.
Produces deployment documentation for operators who maintain network security controls.
limitations: The skill provides SOP guidance and example scripts, not a verified network security product.
The examples may require administrator privileges and can disrupt host networking if run unchanged.
The domain and port lists are generic and must be reviewed for each organization.
The validation commands depend on local firewall, DNS, and proxy behavior.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Claude Code Sandbox Policy
use_cases.description: Define allowed domains, blocked protocols, ports, and documentation before enabling network access for a development sandbox.

use_cases.title: Review CI Network Egress Controls
use_cases.description: Map build dependencies to an allowlist and create repeatable tests for expected outbound access.

use_cases.title: Document Team Network Rules
use_cases.description: Create clear network requirements, deployment notes, and maintenance checks for engineering teams using AI coding tools.

prompt_templates.title: List Network Requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new sandbox
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to list the external domains, ports, protocols, and rate limits needed for my Claude Code sandbox.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Allowlist Policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to draft a whitelist network policy for a project that needs GitHub, package registries, and one internal API.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Safe Validation Steps
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced testing without unsafe live targets
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design network access tests that avoid contacting untrusted domains and preserve existing proxy settings.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Proposed Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my planned firewall, DNS, proxy, and documentation changes before I apply them in a sandbox.

output_examples.input: I need network access rules for a Claude Code sandbox that uses GitHub and package registries.
output_examples.output: A requirements summary with trusted domains, allowed outbound ports, blocked protocols, rate limits, and documentation tasks.

output_examples.input: Review this network isolation plan before I run it.
output_examples.output: A security review that calls out privileged firewall changes, proxy side effects, rollback needs, and safer validation targets.

output_examples.input: Create a maintenance checklist for sandbox network controls.
output_examples.output: A concise checklist covering monthly domain review, weekly log audit, policy tests, and documentation updates.

best_practices: Review every domain, port, and protocol against an approved business requirement before applying rules.
Test firewall, DNS, and proxy changes in a disposable sandbox before using shared infrastructure.
Keep rollback steps and audit notes with every network policy change.
anti_patterns: Running generated firewall scripts on a workstation or shared server without review.
Using public suspicious domains as live test targets for blocked access checks.
Clearing proxy environment variables without confirming organizational egress requirements.

faq.question: Does this skill configure my network automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a guided SOP and example commands that an operator must review before use.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it require administrator privileges?
faq.answer: Some example firewall and system file changes usually require elevated privileges. Test them only in approved environments.

faq.question: Are the trusted domains complete for every project?
faq.answer: No. The listed domains are examples and must be adjusted for each project dependency.

faq.question: How should blocked-domain testing be handled?
faq.answer: Use a controlled test host, reserved domain, or local mock instead of a public suspicious domain.

faq.question: What should I check before publishing a policy?
faq.answer: Confirm business need, proxy behavior, rollback steps, logs, and repeatable validation for each rule.
